title: Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound
exact_target: Does an absolute C exist such that, for all $d,N\geq 1$ and every indexed family $v_{1},\dots ,v_N$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $R^{d}$ with $\Sigma _i$ $v_i=0$, a permutation $\pi $ satisfies $max_{0\leq k\leq N}\Vert \Sigma _{i\leq k}v_(\pi (i))\Vert _{2}\leq C\surd d$? Repetitions and zeros are permitted, and the same C must be independent of N.
